payload.acceptance_criteria: a repository whose config already names the managed core gets no advice line for that file, and a repository that does not still gets it - the second half asserted, or the fix is a suppression rather than a check
payload.description:
When install finishes in a repository that already excludes the managed core from its linters, I want it to say nothing, so I can stop training a consumer to skim the region where a tracked CI edit is also reported.

Found by the terminal canary, filed there as term-ip2wz and pressed after it shipped twice unchanged. scaffolds.install_notes tests only whether a config file exists, never what it contains, so it advises extend-exclude on a .ruff.toml that has carried exactly that for releases. The canary verified the exclusion is genuinely in force rather than merely present: ruff format --check over the managed core exits 0 on 54 files.

The same block tells a consumer to hand-edit .pre-commit-config.yaml in a run that separately reports it has just rewritten that file.

Severity is low and nothing fails. The reason it is worth fixing is where it sits: the advice is the tail of the install output, and the tail is also where a re-pin of a tracked CI workflow is announced. Unactionable boilerplate beside a real edit teaches a reader to skip both.

Recorded against myself: this was already a requirement on basicly-fmgwtwi, which is still open, and I shipped two releases without meeting it while telling the canary it was on the record. It was on the record and it was not done.
payload.requirements: the check reads the file rather than testing its presence. A false skip is possible if the path is named for some other reason, and that is accepted and stated rather than guarded, because the cost of a missed note is one line a consumer can still read in the documentation.
payload.title: read the file before advising a change it already carries

payload.acceptance_criteria: external-facts says the control is built from a failure that has been seen rather than an assumed one, and says to check the denominator moved; the always-on surfaces stay under their caps and the projection gates pass
payload.description:
When an agent runs a positive control and it returns zero, I want the rule to say what the control must be built from, so I can stop reading a control's own zero as confirmation.

Asked for by the terminal canary as term-2vkce, and the request is well founded: the rule is in managed core they may never edit, they followed both halves of it, and still got a false reading. The wording said run a positive control and that if the control is empty too the zero belongs to the probe. It never said what the control must be built from.

Their case is the evidence. They planted a table they called ragged; it was valid compact style, so it was never a violation, reported zero, and read exactly like a dead probe. Rebuilt from the defect actually observed - padded cells over an unpadded delimiter row - it reported two errors. What rescued the diagnosis was the denominator: 151 files became 152 when the control was added, which proved the file was read and sent them to the table rather than the tooling.

Three of my own false zeros the same day were the environment answering instead of the code. Theirs is the subtler one and the one the rule did not cover.

Carrying it in their overlay was the fallback, and the objection to that is right: two copies of one rule drift, and ours is the copy every other consumer reads.
payload.requirements: the amendment sits in the existing bullet rather than adding one, because the always-on budget is a standing cost on every consumer. The token cost declared on the fragment is updated to what the projection measures rather than left to drift.
payload.title: amend the positive control rule with what a control must be built from

payload.acceptance_criteria: the tutorial names a version in the claim and in the install command only; the two transcript lines elide it the way the page already elides a timestamp; the release pins the install command; a release needs one human edit, the claim, and docs-claims still refuses a page whose claim names a stale version
payload.description:
When a patch release changes nothing the tutorial quotes, I want the page to need one edit rather than five, so I can stop paying a ten minute walkthrough for a version string.

Measured across v0.14.0, v0.14.1 and v0.14.2, all cut on 2026-09-18: each required the whole walkthrough re-run - install, scaffold, create, dor, classify, worktree, land, ship, log, status - and every quoted block matched apart from record ids, commit hashes and sub-second timings. Three runs, zero drift found, five strings edited each time.

The five sites are not one kind of thing and the gate cannot tell them apart. Line 7 is the claim, that every command and output was executed on a named version. Lines 36 and 50 are instructions, the uvx line a reader types. Lines 66 and 68 are transcript, what the tool printed.

The page already elides a timestamp on line 68 with its own convention, so eliding the version beside it is consistent rather than new.
payload.requirements: no quoted output is rewritten by a tool: the release may pin an instruction a reader types and may not touch a line the page presents as printed. The claim stays a human edit, because it is the sentence that must be true.
payload.title: stop a patch release costing a full tutorial re-record

payload.description:
A consumer upgrading a repository with basicly install cannot see which of their tracked files the run will touch until it has touched them. The run rewrites the vendored core catalog, the agent instruction files, the skills, the hooks, .gitattributes, .gitignore and the settings deny-list, and it keeps or overwrites a hand-edited core file depending on a recorded hash the consumer cannot read.

A dry run answers one question: which paths does this write, and which of my own edits does it keep. It writes nothing and exits 0.
payload.title: show what basicly install would write before it writes it

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value: Given a repository that already has basicly installed, when I run basicly install --dry-run, then it prints every path the real run would create, overwrite or delete, prints which hand-edited core files it would keep, writes nothing, and exits 0. Verified by taking a checksum of the whole tree before and after the dry run and showing it unchanged, then running the real install and showing every path it changed was named by the dry run.

payload.name: close_reason
payload.value: basicly install wires a post-merge hook that calls basicly tracker fold. The kit's install_hook takes a --command override, so the host's own fold command replaces the kit's compact-and-commit block; the hook prints what to run when the command fails. Validated on a throwaway consumer repo: a branch minted a record into pending-feature.jsonl, main merged it, and the hook folded it into events-0001.jsonl and committed chore(beads): fold pending writer shards into the trunk log (hookv-1sli) with a clean tree.

payload.text: Dirty-tree control run after close: on a throwaway consumer, a branch shard merged into a tree carrying an uncommitted README edit survived as pending-control2.jsonl with no fold commit; the same shard folded into events-0001.jsonl the moment the tree was clean. Both arms of the acceptance criterion observed.

payload.name: close_reason
payload.value: The two transcript lines in docs/tutorial/first-loop.md that named a version now name the tool alone, and docs/tutorial/*.md joined release.PIN_GLOBS. The pin regex matches only @vX.Y.Z, so it re-pins the instruction lines and leaves the single claim on line 7 as the one human edit a release costs.

payload.name: close_reason
payload.value: basicly install --dry-run names every path the run would create, overwrite or delete, and writes nothing. Validated on a throwaway consumer: the path set and the file checksums were byte-identical across a dry run, the real install afterwards changed only paths the dry run named or covered, and a planted drift in AGENTS.md and a projected SKILL.md made it name exactly build and skills-build.

payload.description: Fold the five pending changelog fragments into CHANGELOG.md, bump to 0.15.0, refresh the install pins, regenerate the projections and tag. Two added fragments make this a minor, not a patch.
payload.title: cut basicly 0.15.0

payload.description: basicly release rewrote the version, the pins, the projections and the changelog, then met the docs-claims refusal at the commit gate and restored the tree. The claim it trips on is the one line the pin rewrite cannot move: a transcript that names a bare basicly X.Y.Z. Refuse it in blocking_reasons so --dry-run shows it before any write.
payload.title: refuse a stale tutorial transcript in the release preflight

payload.description: tests/test_supervise_board.py::test_a_tick_emits_a_snapshot_whose_freshness_is_younger_than_the_tick failed once inside basicly verify --mode full on 2026-09-18 with assert 0 <= -1.439611, then passed on the next verify run and 3 of 3 times alone. A negative age means the snapshot timestamp is read as later than the reader's own now, so the assertion compares two clocks rather than one monotonic source. It is a flake in the instrument, not in the board: a red verify on an unrelated lane is the cost.
payload.title: a board freshness test asserts a non-negative age against two clocks

The cut found two defects first: basicly release met the docs-claims tutorial refusal at the commit gate rather than in preflight (fixed as basicly-oror9os), and the post-merge hook resolved the engine at install time, which the canary proved is a certain break rather than a risk since it has no basicly on PATH at all (fixed as part of basicly-z9s4iin).

payload.description: basicly-7407m52 replaced an over-eager exclusion notice with a silent one. _needs_core_exclusion asked whether the config file contains the string .basicly/core anywhere, so a per-file-ignores entry, an include list or a comment naming the path suppresses the advice a repo with no exclusion needs. Reported by the canary with a controlled fixture pair and a v0.14.2 positive control; reproduced here with three rows where the middle one is the defect and the third proves the path is reachable.
payload.title: the core exclusion advice reads a mention not an exclusion

payload.description: The dry run writes nothing, so it does not sync the core catalog, so basicly install --dry-run ran the vendored install_hook.py rather than the one the sync would place. A consumer upgrading from an older version saw unrecognized arguments --command and --advice and the line 'the post-merge hook was not installed', naming the release's headline feature as broken when a real install wires it. A false negative exactly where a consumer cannot check.
payload.title: install --dry-run previews the hook step with the unsynced kit
